## Standards

<a id="PostgresSql"></a>

### PostgreSQL's dialect

`PostgresSql` · `src/sql.ts:71`

How PostgreSQL names the parameters of a statement, types its columns, and knows a table exists.

Source: PostgreSQL: Value Expressions, Positional Parameters ($n); Numeric Types (double precision, integer); Character Types (text); The Information Schema (tables) · `https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-expressions.html#SQL-EXPRESSIONS-PARAMETERS-POSITIONAL`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `parameter` | `$` | Opens a positional parameter: then its position |
| `first` | `1` | The position of the first parameter |
| `text` | `TEXT` | The type of a column of text |
| `number` | `DOUBLE PRECISION` | The type of a column of numbers (an 8-byte floating point number, as SQLite's REAL) |
| `integer` | `INTEGER` | The type of a column of whole numbers (yes or no, as 1 or 0) |
| `exists` | `SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_name = $1` | The name of the table of this name, if there is one |

- Maintained by: trame
- Serves: [Data described once](product.md#DataDescribedOnce)
- Used by: [PostgreSQL's tables](records.md#PostgresTables), [PostgreSQL parameter](#PostgresParameter)
- Defines: [PostgreSQL parameter](#PostgresParameter)

<a id="Sql"></a>

### SQL

`Sql` · `src/sql.ts:15`

The statements the tables of entities need, as SQL defines them and as SQLite and PostgreSQL both read them.

Source: ISO/IEC 9075 (SQL): SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE; CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and ALTER TABLE … RENAME COLUMN, … DROP COLUMN, as SQLite (3.35 on) and PostgreSQL both accept them · `https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-commands.html`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `space` | `" "` | Separates the words of a statement |
| `comma` | `,` | Separates the items of a list (columns, values, definitions) |
| `open` | `(` | Opens a list of columns, of values or of definitions |
| `close` | `)` | Closes it |
| `equals` | `=` | Compares a column with a value, or gives it one |
| `select` | `SELECT` | Reads columns |
| `from` | `FROM` | Names the table read |
| `where` | `WHERE` | Introduces the condition the rows must meet |
| `insertInto` | `INSERT INTO` | Adds a row to a table |
| `values` | `VALUES` | Introduces the values of the row |
| `update` | `UPDATE` | Changes rows of a table |
| `set` | `SET` | Introduces the columns changed |
| `deleteFrom` | `DELETE FROM` | Removes rows of a table |
| `createTable` | `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` | Creates a table, unless it exists |
| `alterTable` | `ALTER TABLE` | Changes a table |
| `addColumn` | `ADD COLUMN` | Gives a table a column, empty in every row |
| `renameColumn` | `RENAME COLUMN` | Gives a column another name, its values kept |
| `to` | `TO` | Introduces the new name |
| `dropColumn` | `DROP COLUMN` | Removes a column, and its values |
| `primaryKey` | `PRIMARY KEY` | The column that identifies a row |
| `notNull` | `NOT NULL` | A column that always has a value |
| `isNull` | `IS NULL` | A column that has no value |
| `references` | `REFERENCES` | A column whose value is the key of a row of another table |
| `countAll` | `count(*)` | The number of rows |
| `as` | `AS` | Names a result column |

- Maintained by: trame
- Serves: [Data described once](product.md#DataDescribedOnce)
- Defines: [A column added](#AddColumn), [Column definition](#ColumnDefinition), [Condition on a column](#ColumnEquals), [A column with no value](#ColumnIsNull), [Count](#CountRows), [Table creation](#CreateTable), [Deletion](#DeleteRows), [A column dropped](#DropColumn), [Insertion](#InsertRow), [A column renamed](#RenameColumn), [Selection](#SelectRows), [List](#SqlList), [Update](#UpdateRows)
- Used by: [A column added](#AddColumn), [Column definition](#ColumnDefinition), [Condition on a column](#ColumnEquals), [A column with no value](#ColumnIsNull), [Count](#CountRows), [Table creation](#CreateTable), [Deletion](#DeleteRows), [A column dropped](#DropColumn), [Insertion](#InsertRow), [A column renamed](#RenameColumn), [Selection](#SelectRows), [List](#SqlList), [Update](#UpdateRows)

<a id="Sqlite"></a>

### SQLite

`Sqlite` · `src/sql.ts:90`

A database in a file, or in memory; its transactions; a connection that refuses to write.

Source: SQLite: In-Memory Databases; SQL As Understood By SQLite (BEGIN, COMMIT, ROLLBACK); Pragma statements (query_only) · `https://www.sqlite.org/inmemorydb.html`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `memory` | `:memory:` | The name that opens a database in memory, new each time |
| `begin` | `BEGIN` | Starts a transaction |
| `commit` | `COMMIT` | Makes its writes last |
| `rollback` | `ROLLBACK` | Undoes them |
| `readOnly` | `PRAGMA query_only = ON` | From here on, the connection refuses any statement that would change the database |
| `readWrite` | `PRAGMA query_only = OFF` | From here on, it accepts them again |

- Maintained by: trame
- Serves: [Data described once](product.md#DataDescribedOnce)
- Used by: [SQLite in memory](records.md#SqliteInMemory)

<a id="SqliteSql"></a>

### SQLite's dialect

`SqliteSql` · `src/sql.ts:53`

How SQLite names the parameters of a statement, types its columns, and knows a table exists.

Source: SQLite: SQL As Understood By SQLite, Parameters (?); Datatypes In SQLite (TEXT, REAL, INTEGER); The Schema Table (sqlite_schema) · `https://www.sqlite.org/lang_expr.html#varparam`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `parameter` | `?` | A parameter: the next value given with the statement |
| `text` | `TEXT` | The type of a column of text |
| `number` | `REAL` | The type of a column of numbers (an 8-byte floating point number) |
| `integer` | `INTEGER` | The type of a column of whole numbers (yes or no, as 1 or 0) |
| `exists` | `SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = ?` | The name of the table of this name, if there is one |
